_comment: THE CATALOGUE. Authoritative list of every language LangKraft will ever ship.
It lived only in a conversation until 2026-10-05, and was lost. It is here now so
that it cannot be lost again. Nothing in the pipeline, the app or the tests may
hard-code a language list; they all read this file.
English is `role: calibration`: it measures whether the tier sizes are right and is
structurally not a travel aid, so it is in the catalogue but is not one of the 20.
Tatoeba English-pivot sentence-pair counts are recorded because they decide whether a
language can be attested-sourced at all. `null` means NOT YET MEASURED -- which is a
gap to close, not a zero.

MEASURED 2026-10-05: all 21 languages have an English-pivot bitext of 1000+ sentences or the API cap. 1000 means the API's ceiling, not the true count. Serbian (srp), Dari (fas), Persian (pes) and MSA Arabic (arb) were each confirmed at the cap, so no language in the catalogue is blocked on attestation.

TATOEBA CODES ARE NOT ISO 639-3. `tatoeba_code` overrides the catalogue code when querying the source, and was added after a false measurement. Dari is `fas` here (correct ISO 639-3, and correct for the app's own identifiers) but `pes` at Tatoeba -- `fas` is not a language the site knows, and `?from=fas` or `?to=fas` returns English sentences with no Dari in them while still reporting count=1000. An earlier claim that Dari had 1000+ attested pairs was that false reading, not a real corpus.

languages.name: Dari
languages.tatoeba_en_pairs_note: MEASURED 2026-10-06 under the code that actually filters. A FLOOR, not a total: 81 Persian pairs verified across 20 core concepts from the FIRST page of results only, and every count was verified by reading the Persian text back out of the response rather than trusting the API. The API's own total for those same 20 queries is 1165.
languages.tatoeba_code_note: Tatoeba HAS NO DARI. Verified, not assumed: `prs` (the Dari code) reports 721 results and returns zero Dari, substituting an unrelated scatter of languages — it does not filter, exactly as `fas` does not. `pes` is the only Persian-family code that filters, verified by every result it returns carrying lang_tag=pes and nothing else. `pes` is IRANIAN Persian. Dari is the Afghan variety of the same language: mutually intelligible, not identical. Filling the Dari tier from `pes` is therefore a product decision about labelling, not a harvesting fix, and is NOT done automatically.

note_phrasebook_reading_script: Optional. 'own' means the phrasebook writes its reading in the language's own script rather than transliterated. Only Dari does: the page writes the phrase in Latin and the Dari in Arabic script inside the italics, so a parser requiring a Latin reading rejects every phrase on it. Measured on the harvested page: 54 rows, 0 with a reading, before this was recorded; the whole page was unusable. Left out of the code as a set of language codes precisely so that adding a language never means editing the parser.
